    if num_clusters > 1 and num_customers > 1:
        # Improved clustering that considers both spatial proximity and capacity constraints
        # Start with depot-adjacent customers and build clusters incrementally
        
        # Calculate distances from depot to each customer
        depot_distances = distance_matrix[0, 1:]  # Distances from depot to all customers
        
        # Initialize clusters with closest customers to depot
        cluster_centers = []
        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        # Process customers in order of proximity to depot
        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():
            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')
            
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members
                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
    else:
        # No clustering needed, all customers in one cluster
        pass
    
    # Create cluster assignment tensor for all nodes (with depot at index 0)
    all_cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments
    
    # Create a symmetric matrix indicating whether pairs are in same cluster
    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()
    
    # Base similarity matrix (inverse of distances with small epsilon)
    eps = 1e-8
    inv_distances = 1.0 / (distance_matrix + eps)
    
    # Boost similarity for same-cluster pairs
    intra_cluster_weight = 2.0
    clustered_similarities = inv_distances * (1.0 + (intra_cluster_weight - 1.0) * cluster_mask)
    
    # Add depot connection bonuses
    depot_bonus = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    depot_customer_strength = demands[1:] * 1.5  # Higher demand customers get bigger bonus to depot
    depot_bonus[0, 1:] = depot_customer_strength
    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)
    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2
    
    # Create penalty for long-distance customer-to-customer edges
    long_edge_penalty = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    customer_to_customer_mask = torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Efficient implementation of attention bias for CVRP POMO.
    
    The algorithm:
    1. Uses simple greedy clustering based on spatial proximity and demand
    2. Creates cluster-based biases to encourage local routing
    3. Adds depot connectivity bonuses
    4. Applies capacity-based penalties
    5. Balances all factors efficiently
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: Tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all nodes (depot + customers)
        demands: Tensor of shape (n,) representing normalized demands for each node (0 for depot)
        
    Returns:
        Tensor of shape (n, n) with attention bias values (higher for desirable edges)
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    device = distance_matrix.device
    
    # Handle small instances
    if n <= 2:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Extract customer info (excluding depot at index 0)
    customer_distances = distance_matrix[1:, 1:]  # (n-1, n-1)
    customer_demands = demands[1:]  # (n-1,)
    num_customers = n - 1
    
    # Simple clustering based on k-means-like approach for efficiency
    # Number of clusters based on total demand and capacity
    total_demand = customer_demands.sum().item()
    estimated_vehicles = max(1, int(np.ceil(total_demand)))
    num_clusters = min(max(2, estimated_vehicles), num_customers)
    
    # Initialize cluster assignments
    cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(num_customers, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    
    if num_clusters > 1 and num_customers > 1:
        # Improved clustering that considers both spatial proximity and capacity constraints
        # Start with depot-adjacent customers and build clusters incrementally
        
        # Calculate distances from depot to each customer
        depot_distances = distance_matrix[0, 1:]  # Distances from depot to all customers
        
        # Initialize clusters with closest customers to depot
        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        # Process customers in order of proximity to depot
        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():

                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')
            
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members

                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance

    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()

        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        # Process customers in order of proximity to depot
        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():
            if len(unassigned_customers) == 0:
                break
                
            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer
            valid_clusters = []
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    valid_clusters.append(c_idx)
            
            if valid_clusters:
                # Choose the cluster with the smallest current demand to balance loads
                chosen_cluster = min(valid_clusters, key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            else:
                # If no cluster can fit this customer, assign to the cluster that violates capacity least
                chosen_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), 
                                   key=lambda c: max(0, cluster_demands[c] + customer_demands[customer_idx] - 1.0))
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = chosen_cluster
            cluster_demands[chosen_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
            
            # If unassigned customers are too far, we might need to start new clusters
            # But since we're constrained by num_clusters, we'll just assign remaining customers
            # to the least loaded cluster that can take them
            if len(unassigned_customers) > 0:
                # For any remaining customers, assign them to the best available cluster
                for remaining_idx in unassigned_customers:
                    valid_clusters = [c for c in range(num_clusters) 
                                    if cluster_demands[c] + customer_demands[remaining_idx] <= 1.2]  # Allow slight over-capacity
                    if valid_clusters:
                        chosen_cluster = min(valid_clusters, key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
                    else:
                        chosen_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
                    
                    cluster_assignments[remaining_idx] = chosen_cluster
                    cluster_demands[chosen_cluster] += customer_demands[remaining_idx]

                                best_cluster = c_idx

    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]

    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2

    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Efficient implementation of attention bias for CVRP POMO.
    
    The algorithm:
    1. Uses simple greedy clustering based on spatial proximity and demand
    2. Creates cluster-based biases to encourage local routing
    3. Adds depot connectivity bonuses
    4. Applies capacity-based penalties
    5. Balances all factors efficiently
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: Tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all nodes (depot + customers)
        demands: Tensor of shape (n,) representing normalized demands for each node (0 for depot)
        
    Returns:
        Tensor of shape (n, n) with attention bias values (higher for desirable edges)
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    device = distance_matrix.device
    
    # Handle small instances
    if n <= 2:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Extract customer info (excluding depot at index 0)
    customer_distances = distance_matrix[1:, 1:]  # (n-1, n-1)
    customer_demands = demands[1:]  # (n-1,)
    num_customers = n - 1
    
    # Simple clustering based on k-means-like approach for efficiency
    # Number of clusters based on total demand and capacity
    total_demand = customer_demands.sum().item()
    estimated_vehicles = max(1, int(np.ceil(total_demand)))
    num_clusters = min(max(2, estimated_vehicles), num_customers)
    
    # Initialize cluster assignments
    cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(num_customers, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    
    if num_clusters > 1 and num_customers > 1:
        # Improved clustering that considers both spatial proximity and capacity constraints
        # Start with depot-adjacent customers and build clusters incrementally
        
        # Calculate distances from depot to each customer
        depot_distances = distance_matrix[0, 1:]  # Distances from depot to all customers
        
        # Initialize clusters with closest customers to depot
        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        # Process customers in order of proximity to depot
        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():
            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')
            
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members
                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
    else:
        # No clustering needed, all customers in one cluster
        pass
    
    # Create cluster assignment tensor for all nodes (with depot at index 0)
    all_cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments
    
    # Create a symmetric matrix indicating whether pairs are in same cluster
    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()
    
    # Base similarity matrix (inverse of distances with small epsilon)
    eps = 1e-8
    inv_distances = 1.0 / (distance_matrix + eps)
    
    # Boost similarity for same-cluster pairs
    intra_cluster_weight = 2.0
    clustered_similarities = inv_distances * (1.0 + (intra_cluster_weight - 1.0) * cluster_mask)

    depot_bonus = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    depot_customer_strength = demands[1:] * 1.5  # Higher demand customers get bigger bonus to depot
    depot_bonus[0, 1:] = depot_customer_strength
    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)
    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2
    
    # Create penalty for long-distance customer-to-customer edges
    long_edge_penalty = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    customer_to_customer_mask = torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    valid_clusters.append(c_idx)
            
            if valid_clusters:
                # Choose the cluster with the smallest current demand to balance loads
                chosen_cluster = min(valid_clusters, key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            else:
                # If no cluster can fit this customer, assign to the cluster that violates capacity least
                chosen_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), 
                                   key=lambda c: max(0, cluster_demands[c] + customer_demands[customer_idx] - 1.0))
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = chosen_cluster
            cluster_demands[chosen_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
            
            # If unassigned customers are too far, we might need to start new clusters
            # But since we're constrained by num_clusters, we'll just assign remaining customers
            # to the least loaded cluster that can take them
            if len(unassigned_customers) > 0:
                # For any remaining customers, assign them to the best available cluster
                for remaining_idx in unassigned_customers:
                    valid_clusters = [c for c in range(num_clusters) 
                                    if cluster_demands[c] + customer_demands[remaining_idx] <= 1.2]  # Allow slight over-capacity
                    if valid_clusters:
                        chosen_cluster = min(valid_clusters, key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
                    else:
                        chosen_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
                    
                    cluster_assignments[remaining_idx] = chosen_cluster
                    cluster_demands[chosen_cluster] += customer_demands[remaining_idx]
            
            break  # Break after processing the main assignment loop
    else:
        # No clustering needed, all customers in one cluster
    cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(num_customers, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    
    if num_clusters > 1 and num_customers > 1:
        # Improved clustering that considers both spatial proximity and capacity constraints
        # Start with depot-adjacent customers and build clusters incrementally
        
        # Calculate distances from depot to each customer
        depot_distances = distance_matrix[0, 1:]  # Distances from depot to all customers
        
        # Initialize clusters with closest customers to depot
        cluster_centers = []
        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        # Process customers in order of proximity to depot
        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():
            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')
            
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members
                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
    else:

        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)

            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')

                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members
                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]

        pass

    all_cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments

    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()

    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)

    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]

    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2

    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

import torch
import numpy as np

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Efficient implementation of attention bias for CVRP POMO.
    
    The algorithm:
    1. Uses simple greedy clustering based on spatial proximity and demand
    2. Creates cluster-based biases to encourage local routing
    3. Adds depot connectivity bonuses
    4. Applies capacity-based penalties
    5. Balances all factors efficiently
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: Tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all nodes (depot + customers)
        demands: Tensor of shape (n,) representing normalized demands for each node (0 for depot)
        
    Returns:
        Tensor of shape (n, n) with attention bias values (higher for desirable edges)
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    device = distance_matrix.device
    
    # Handle small instances
    if n <= 2:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Extract customer info (excluding depot at index 0)
    customer_distances = distance_matrix[1:, 1:]  # (n-1, n-1)
    customer_demands = demands[1:]  # (n-1,)
    num_customers = n - 1
    
    # Simple clustering based on k-means-like approach for efficiency
    # Number of clusters based on total demand and capacity
    total_demand = customer_demands.sum().item()
    estimated_vehicles = max(1, int(np.ceil(total_demand)))
    num_clusters = min(max(2, estimated_vehicles), num_customers)
    
    cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(num_customers, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    
    if num_clusters > 1 and num_customers > 1:
        # Improved clustering that considers both spatial proximity and capacity constraints
        # Start with depot-adjacent customers and build clusters incrementally
        
        # Calculate distances from depot to each customer
        depot_distances = distance_matrix[0, 1:]  # Distances from depot to all customers
        
        # Initialize clusters with closest customers to depot
        cluster_centers = []
        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        # Process customers in order of proximity to depot
        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():
            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')
            
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members
                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
    else:
        # No clustering needed, all customers in one cluster
        pass
    
    # Create cluster assignment tensor for all nodes (with depot at index 0)
    all_cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments
    
    # Create a symmetric matrix indicating whether pairs are in same cluster
    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()
    
    # Base similarity matrix (inverse of distances with small epsilon)
    eps = 1e-8
    inv_distances = 1.0 / (distance_matrix + eps)
    
    # Boost similarity for same-cluster pairs
    intra_cluster_weight = 2.0
    clustered_similarities = inv_distances * (1.0 + (intra_cluster_weight - 1.0) * cluster_mask)
    
    # Add depot connection bonuses
    depot_bonus = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    depot_customer_strength = demands[1:] * 1.5  # Higher demand customers get bigger bonus to depot
    depot_bonus[0, 1:] = depot_customer_strength
    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)
    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2
    
    # Create penalty for long-distance customer-to-customer edges
    long_edge_penalty = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    customer_to_customer_mask = torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Efficient implementation of attention bias for CVRP POMO.
    
    The algorithm:
    1. Uses simple greedy clustering based on spatial proximity and demand
    2. Creates cluster-based biases to encourage local routing
    3. Adds depot connectivity bonuses
    4. Applies capacity-based penalties
    5. Balances all factors efficiently
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: Tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all nodes (depot + customers)
        demands: Tensor of shape (n,) representing normalized demands for each node (0 for depot)
        
    Returns:
        Tensor of shape (n, n) with attention bias values (higher for desirable edges)
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    device = distance_matrix.device
    
    # Handle small instances
    if n <= 2:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Extract customer info (excluding depot at index 0)
    customer_distances = distance_matrix[1:, 1:]  # (n-1, n-1)
    customer_demands = demands[1:]  # (n-1,)
    num_customers = n - 1
    
    # Simple clustering based on k-means-like approach for efficiency
    # Number of clusters based on total demand and capacity
    total_demand = customer_demands.sum().item()
    estimated_vehicles = max(1, int(np.ceil(total_demand)))
    num_clusters = min(max(2, estimated_vehicles), num_customers)
    
    cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(num_customers, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    
    if num_clusters > 1 and num_customers > 1:
        # Improved clustering that considers both spatial proximity and capacity constraints
        # Start with depot-adjacent customers and build clusters incrementally
        
        # Calculate distances from depot to each customer
        depot_distances = distance_matrix[0, 1:]  # Distances from depot to all customers
        
        # Initialize clusters with closest customers to depot
        cluster_centers = []
        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():
            if len(unassigned_customers) == 0:
                break
                
            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer
            valid_clusters = []
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    valid_clusters.append(c_idx)
            
            if valid_clusters:
                # Choose the cluster with the smallest current demand to balance loads
                chosen_cluster = min(valid_clusters, key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            else:
                # If no cluster can fit this customer, assign to the cluster that violates capacity least
                chosen_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), 
                                   key=lambda c: max(0, cluster_demands[c] + customer_demands[customer_idx] - 1.0))
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = chosen_cluster
            cluster_demands[chosen_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
            
            # If unassigned customers are too far, we might need to start new clusters
            # But since we're constrained by num_clusters, we'll just assign remaining customers
            # to the least loaded cluster that can take them
            if len(unassigned_customers) > 0:
                # For any remaining customers, assign them to the best available cluster
                for remaining_idx in unassigned_customers:
                    valid_clusters = [c for c in range(num_clusters) 
                                    if cluster_demands[c] + customer_demands[remaining_idx] <= 1.2]  # Allow slight over-capacity
                    if valid_clusters:
                        chosen_cluster = min(valid_clusters, key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
                    else:
                        chosen_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
                    
                    cluster_assignments[remaining_idx] = chosen_cluster
                    cluster_demands[chosen_cluster] += customer_demands[remaining_idx]
            
            break  # Break after processing the main assignment loop
    else:

            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1

                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break

                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()

                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx

            if best_cluster == -1:

    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments

    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength

    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2

    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)

    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]

                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
    else:
        # No clustering needed, all customers in one cluster
        pass
    
    # Create cluster assignment tensor for all nodes (with depot at index 0)
    all_cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments
    
    # Create a symmetric matrix indicating whether pairs are in same cluster
    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()
    
    # Base similarity matrix (inverse of distances with small epsilon)
    eps = 1e-8
    inv_distances = 1.0 / (distance_matrix + eps)
    
    # Boost similarity for same-cluster pairs
    intra_cluster_weight = 2.0
    clustered_similarities = inv_distances * (1.0 + (intra_cluster_weight - 1.0) * cluster_mask)
    
    # Add depot connection bonuses
    depot_bonus = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    depot_customer_strength = demands[1:] * 1.5  # Higher demand customers get bigger bonus to depot
    depot_bonus[0, 1:] = depot_customer_strength
    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)
    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2
    
    # Create penalty for long-distance customer-to-customer edges
    long_edge_penalty = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    customer_to_customer_mask = torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Efficient implementation of attention bias for CVRP POMO.
    
    The algorithm:
    1. Uses simple greedy clustering based on spatial proximity and demand
    2. Creates cluster-based biases to encourage local routing
    3. Adds depot connectivity bonuses
    4. Applies capacity-based penalties
    5. Balances all factors efficiently
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: Tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all nodes (depot + customers)
        demands: Tensor of shape (n,) representing normalized demands for each node (0 for depot)

    depot_bonus = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    depot_customer_strength = demands[1:] * 1.5  # Higher demand customers get bigger bonus to depot
    depot_bonus[0, 1:] = depot_customer_strength
    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)
    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2
    
    # Create penalty for long-distance customer-to-customer edges
    long_edge_penalty = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    customer_to_customer_mask = torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

import torch
import numpy as np

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Efficient implementation of attention bias for CVRP POMO.
    
    The algorithm:
    1. Uses simple greedy clustering based on spatial proximity and demand
    2. Creates cluster-based biases to encourage local routing
    3. Adds depot connectivity bonuses
    4. Applies capacity-based penalties
    5. Balances all factors efficiently
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: Tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all nodes (depot + customers)
        demands: Tensor of shape (n,) representing normalized demands for each node (0 for depot)
        
    Returns:
        Tensor of shape (n, n) with attention bias values (higher for desirable edges)
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    device = distance_matrix.device
    
    # Handle small instances
    if n <= 2:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Extract customer info (excluding depot at index 0)
    customer_distances = distance_matrix[1:, 1:]  # (n-1, n-1)
    customer_demands = demands[1:]  # (n-1,)
    num_customers = n - 1
    
    # Simple clustering based on k-means-like approach for efficiency
    # Number of clusters based on total demand and capacity
    total_demand = customer_demands.sum().item()
    estimated_vehicles = max(1, int(np.ceil(total_demand)))
    num_clusters = min(max(2, estimated_vehicles), num_customers)
    
    cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(num_customers, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    
    if num_clusters > 1 and num_customers > 1:
        # Improved clustering that considers both spatial proximity and capacity constraints
        # Start with depot-adjacent customers and build clusters incrementally
        
        # Calculate distances from depot to each customer
        depot_distances = distance_matrix[0, 1:]  # Distances from depot to all customers
        
        # Initialize clusters with closest customers to depot
        cluster_centers = []
        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        # Process customers in order of proximity to depot
        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():
            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')
            
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members
                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
    else:
        # No clustering needed, all customers in one cluster
        pass
    
    # Create cluster assignment tensor for all nodes (with depot at index 0)
    all_cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments
    
    # Create a symmetric matrix indicating whether pairs are in same cluster
    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()
    
    # Base similarity matrix (inverse of distances with small epsilon)
    eps = 1e-8
    inv_distances = 1.0 / (distance_matrix + eps)
    
    # Boost similarity for same-cluster pairs
    intra_cluster_weight = 2.0
    clustered_similarities = inv_distances * (1.0 + (intra_cluster_weight - 1.0) * cluster_mask)
    
    # Add depot connection bonuses
    depot_bonus = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    depot_customer_strength = demands[1:] * 1.5  # Higher demand customers get bigger bonus to depot
    depot_bonus[0, 1:] = depot_customer_strength
    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)
    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2
    
    # Create penalty for long-distance customer-to-customer edges
    long_edge_penalty = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    customer_to_customer_mask = torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

    2. Creates cluster-based biases to encourage local routing
    3. Adds depot connectivity bonuses

            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')
            
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members
                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
    else:
        # No clustering needed, all customers in one cluster
        pass
    
    # Create cluster assignment tensor for all nodes (with depot at index 0)
    all_cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments
    
    # Create a symmetric matrix indicating whether pairs are in same cluster
    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()
    
    # Base similarity matrix (inverse of distances with small epsilon)
    eps = 1e-8
    inv_distances = 1.0 / (distance_matrix + eps)
    
    # Boost similarity for same-cluster pairs
    intra_cluster_weight = 2.0
    clustered_similarities = inv_distances * (1.0 + (intra_cluster_weight - 1.0) * cluster_mask)
    
    # Add depot connection bonuses
    depot_bonus = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    depot_customer_strength = demands[1:] * 1.5  # Higher demand customers get bigger bonus to depot
    depot_bonus[0, 1:] = depot_customer_strength
    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)
    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2
    
    # Create penalty for long-distance customer-to-customer edges
    long_edge_penalty = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    customer_to_customer_mask = torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias

import torch
import numpy as np

def heuristics(distance_matrix: torch.Tensor, demands: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Efficient implementation of attention bias for CVRP POMO.
    
    The algorithm:
    1. Uses simple greedy clustering based on spatial proximity and demand
    2. Creates cluster-based biases to encourage local routing
    3. Adds depot connectivity bonuses
    4. Applies capacity-based penalties
    5. Balances all factors efficiently
    
    Args:
        distance_matrix: Tensor of shape (n, n) representing distances between all nodes (depot + customers)
        demands: Tensor of shape (n,) representing normalized demands for each node (0 for depot)
        
    Returns:
        Tensor of shape (n, n) with attention bias values (higher for desirable edges)
    """
    n = distance_matrix.size(0)
    device = distance_matrix.device
    
    # Handle small instances
    if n <= 2:
        return torch.zeros_like(distance_matrix)
    
    # Extract customer info (excluding depot at index 0)
    customer_distances = distance_matrix[1:, 1:]  # (n-1, n-1)
    customer_demands = demands[1:]  # (n-1,)
    num_customers = n - 1
    
    # Simple clustering based on k-means-like approach for efficiency
    # Number of clusters based on total demand and capacity
    total_demand = customer_demands.sum().item()
    estimated_vehicles = max(1, int(np.ceil(total_demand)))
    num_clusters = min(max(2, estimated_vehicles), num_customers)
    
    cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(num_customers, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    
    if num_clusters > 1 and num_customers > 1:
        # Improved clustering that considers both spatial proximity and capacity constraints
        # Start with depot-adjacent customers and build clusters incrementally
        
        # Calculate distances from depot to each customer
        depot_distances = distance_matrix[0, 1:]  # Distances from depot to all customers
        
        # Initialize clusters with closest customers to depot
        cluster_centers = []
        unassigned_customers = set(range(num_customers))
        
        # Assign customers to clusters based on proximity to initial centers and capacity constraints
        cluster_demands = torch.zeros(num_clusters, device=device)
        
        # Process customers in order of proximity to depot
        sorted_by_depot_dist = torch.argsort(depot_distances)
        
        for customer_idx in sorted_by_depot_dist.tolist():
            if customer_idx not in unassigned_customers:
                continue
                
            # Find the cluster that can best accommodate this customer while considering spatial proximity
            # First, calculate distances to all current cluster members to find the best fit
            best_cluster = -1
            min_avg_distance = float('inf')
            
            for c_idx in range(num_clusters):
                # Check if adding this customer would exceed capacity
                if cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.0:
                    # Calculate average distance to existing members of this cluster
                    cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                    
                    if len(cluster_member_indices) == 0:
                        # Empty cluster, just assign this customer
                        best_cluster = c_idx
                        min_avg_distance = 0
                        break
                    else:
                        # Calculate average distance to existing members
                        distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                        avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                        
                        if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                            min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                            best_cluster = c_idx
                else:
                    # Check if we can still add with slight capacity violation (soft constraint)
                    if (cluster_demands[c_idx] + customer_demands[customer_idx] <= 1.2 and 
                        best_cluster == -1):  # Only if no valid cluster found yet
                        cluster_member_indices = (cluster_assignments == c_idx).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                        if len(cluster_member_indices) > 0:
                            distances_to_cluster = customer_distances[customer_idx, cluster_member_indices]
                            avg_distance = distances_to_cluster.mean().item()
                            
                            if avg_distance < min_avg_distance:
                                min_avg_distance = avg_distance
                                best_cluster = c_idx
            
            # If no suitable cluster found, assign to the least loaded cluster
            if best_cluster == -1:
                best_cluster = min(range(num_clusters), key=lambda c: cluster_demands[c])
            
            cluster_assignments[customer_idx] = best_cluster
            cluster_demands[best_cluster] += customer_demands[customer_idx]
            unassigned_customers.discard(customer_idx)
    else:
        # No clustering needed, all customers in one cluster
        pass
    
    # Create cluster assignment tensor for all nodes (with depot at index 0)
    all_cluster_assignments = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    all_cluster_assignments[1:] = cluster_assignments
    
    # Create a symmetric matrix indicating whether pairs are in same cluster
    cluster_mask = (all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(0) == all_cluster_assignments.unsqueeze(1)).float()
    
    # Base similarity matrix (inverse of distances with small epsilon)
    eps = 1e-8
    inv_distances = 1.0 / (distance_matrix + eps)
    
    # Boost similarity for same-cluster pairs
    intra_cluster_weight = 2.0
    clustered_similarities = inv_distances * (1.0 + (intra_cluster_weight - 1.0) * cluster_mask)
    
    # Add depot connection bonuses
    depot_bonus = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    depot_customer_strength = demands[1:] * 1.5  # Higher demand customers get bigger bonus to depot
    depot_bonus[0, 1:] = depot_customer_strength
    depot_bonus[1:, 0] = depot_customer_strength
    
    # Distance-based penalties for very long edges (subtour prevention)
    # Compute distance threshold based on statistics
    non_diag_distances = distance_matrix[~torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)]
    dist_median = torch.median(non_diag_distances)
    dist_threshold = dist_median * 1.2  # Penalize longer than median * 1.2
    
    # Create penalty for long-distance customer-to-customer edges
    long_edge_penalty = torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities)
    customer_to_customer_mask = torch.ones((n, n), dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    customer_to_customer_mask[0, :] = False  # Exclude depot row
    customer_to_customer_mask[:, 0] = False  # Exclude depot column
    
    long_edges = (distance_matrix > dist_threshold) & customer_to_customer_mask
    long_edge_penalty = torch.where(long_edges, -0.5, torch.zeros_like(long_edge_penalty))
    
    # Capacity-aware penalties (vectorized)
    # Penalize edges between high-demand customers that might cause capacity issues
    demand_sum = demands.unsqueeze(0) + demands.unsqueeze(1)  # (n, n)
    capacity_exceeded = (demand_sum > 1.0) & customer_to_customer_mask
    capacity_penalty = torch.where(capacity_exceeded, -(demand_sum - 1.0) * 2.0, 
                                   torch.zeros_like(clustered_similarities))
    
    # Combine all components
    final_bias = clustered_similarities + depot_bonus + long_edge_penalty + capacity_penalty
    
    # Zero out diagonal to prevent self-loops
    final_bias.fill_diagonal_(0)
    
    return final_bias
